newsitem.title: USA: Future murky for Hollywood's closet after "Ellen".
newsitem.headline: Future murky for Hollywood's closet after "Ellen".

text.p: Wednesday's episode of the U.S. sitcom 'Ellen' garnered sky-high ratings, but Hollywood insiders were divided on Thursday as to whether "coming-out" as lesbians will hurt the careers of the show's star, Ellen DeGeneres, and her new real-life girlfriend, Anne Heche.
"Viewers embraced the show's creativity," an ecstatic ABC network said of the episode watched by an estimated 42 million people -- the highest ratings for an ABC programme this year.
The ratings showed that among adults ages 18-49 43 percent of all sets in use on Wednesday night were tuned to "Ellen".

"Ellen and her team, who to their credit endeavoured to take on such weighty subject matter, did so with skill, class and an incredible sense of humour," said the statement by ABC Entertainment President Jamie Tarses.

In the show, which was hyped for months by the network, DeGeneres' character came to the realisation that she was a lesbian. The comedienne herself came out last month and named Heche, star of the current hit "Volcano," as her lover.
Despite making television history by featuring the first openly gay lead character, it also raised questions in Hollywood on the effect being openly gay may have on careers.
Heche currently stars in "Volcano" and there are reports that 20th Century Fox was anxious that the actress' public declaration might hurt the $100 million-movie's box-office.
But the film erupted on its opening weekend, topping box office charts with $14.7 million in ticket sales.
There was more concern however over Heche's next movie, a romantic comedy, "6 Days, 7 Nights" opposite Harrison Ford.
Roger Birnbaum, chairman of Caravan Pictures, took the unusual step of denying in a statement that Ford was upset with the casting now that Heche is openly gay.

"This is disaster time, and poor Harrison Ford is in a no-win situation," one long-time Hollywood agent and publicist told Reuters. "If he doesn't do love scenes (with Heche), he's in for a terrible time as far as prejudice.

"It's a turn-off. I think this will come back to haunt her," said the Hollywood insider who requested anonymity. "(Singer) K.D. Lang didn't flaunt it, I think it will cost her (Heche) her career," he said.
Thomas White, an artists' rights expert in Hollywood, said that audience credibility will be tested.
Ultimately, he said, "economics will prevail" -- meaning that if people stop going to Heche movies or watching DeGeneres' TV shows because they object to lesbianism, the stars' careers will suffer.
